key_insight: Evaluator bias can spread across multi-agent LLM systems, and this propagation can be measured as a contagion effect that remains nontrivial even when all agents use the same base model.
engineering_relevance: For multi-agent AI pipelines, committee-based evaluation and bias-aware network design can materially reduce systematic error propagation and improve reliability.
method: Define a Cross-Agent Contagion Matrix (Gamma_N) to quantify bias transfer between agents.
Run a controlled 3-agent DeepSeek-chat experiment with three evaluator profiles: structured, balanced, and evidence-based.
Compare contagion under different committee sizes and relate regimes to the spectral radius rho(Gamma_N).
evidence_signal: In the 3-agent experiment, contagion coefficients fell in the range gamma = 0.157 to 0.352, and increasing evaluator committee size from k=1 to k=3 reduced effective contagion by 72.4%.
watch_item: The findings come from a controlled setup with one model family and a small agent count, so broader generalization to larger, heterogeneous systems still needs validation.
paper_title: Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
